answers.question: What was the task?
answers.answer: The task was to rename the server timeout setting so its name shows that it is in milliseconds.
quotes: The task was to rename the server timeout setting so that its name shows milliseconds.

answers.question: How did it end: what is done and what is not?
answers.answer: The rename is done in the code and in our settings file and both tests pass, while the operations team's production file still sets the timeout under the old name and was left alone because changes to it go through operations.
quotes: That is done in the code and in our settings file, and both tests pass.
One thing is left.
The operations team's production file still sets the timeout under the old name.
I left that file alone, because changes to it go through operations.

answers.question: How does the thing that changed work?
answers.answer: The code now reads only the new name and falls back to five seconds when it is missing, our settings file gives three seconds under the new name, and production loads our settings file with the operations file on top of it.
quotes: The code now reads only the new name.
When the name is missing, it falls back to five seconds.
Our settings file gives three seconds under the new name.
Production loads our settings file and puts the operations file on top of it.

answers.question: What is the problem, and what causes it?
answers.answer: After the release production would wait three seconds instead of ten, because the operations file sets ten seconds under the old name, which the code no longer reads, so production gets the three seconds from our file.
quotes: The code no longer reads that name, so after the release production waits three seconds instead of ten.
The operations file sets ten seconds under the old name.
Nobody reads that name now.
So production gets our three seconds.

answers.question: What is not verified?
answers.answer: The author did not see the loading of the files in production and knows of the operations file overriding ours only from a code comment, and the tests do not read the production file.
quotes: I know this from a comment in the code; I did not see the loading itself.
They do not read the production file.

answers.question: What do I have to decide, and what does each option give and cost?
answers.answer: The reader decides whether operations rename their line to the new name before the release, which gives one name everywhere with nothing to clean up but makes the release wait for operations, or the code also reads the old name with the old name winning while set, which lets the release go now with production keeping ten seconds but leaves two names in the code until operations rename and the author removes the old one; the author recommends asking operations first.
quotes: You decide whether operations rename their line first, or the code keeps reading the old name for a while.
1. Operations rename their line to the new name before the release
+ one name everywhere, nothing to clean up later
- the release waits for the operations team
2. The code also reads the old name, and the old name wins while it is set
+ the release can go now, and production keeps ten seconds
- two names live in the code until operations rename their line and I remove the old one
I would ask operations first: it is one line for them, and nothing is left to remove later.
